status_summary: The Space Force released a planning framework on 2025-04-17 that describes offensive counterspace options (orbital strike, space link interdiction and terrestrial strike) alongside defensive ones. The FY2026 NDAA (P.L. 119-60, enacted 2025-12-18) added 10 U.S.C. 2275d (Sec. 1603), requiring space systems intended primarily for space warfighting and control to be acquired and operated to meet combatant commander requirements, and raised the Space Force general officer limit from 21 to 24 (Sec. 502), with further Space Force general officer management provisions in Sec. 501. EO 14369 (signed 2025-12-18) directs the government to be able to detect, characterize and counter threats to U.S. space interests from very low Earth orbit through cislunar space and does not mention offensive capabilities, space control or the Space Force. CRS puts the FY2027 Space Force request at about 71.3 billion dollars, including 12.1 billion in anticipated mandatory funding, against 31.9 billion enacted for FY2026, with 2,800 more military personnel, and a trade report puts space control at 21.6 billion; the request is not enacted. EO 14423 (signed 2026-08-28) created a NASA-chaired commission to advise within 120 days on a proposed NASA-led U.S. Space Academy. No source was found on declassification of space threat information or on a Space Force academy.

timeline.event: Space Force releases the Space Warfighting framework describing orbital, link and terrestrial offensive counterspace options.
EO 14369 signed: ability to detect, characterize and counter threats from very low Earth orbit through cislunar space; it does not mention offensive capabilities or the Space Force.

The FY2026 NDAA becomes law as P.L. 119-60. Per the U.S. Code, Sec. 1603 adds 10 U.S.C. 2275d, requiring the Secretary of Defense to acquire and operate space systems intended primarily for space warfighting and control to meet combatant commander requirements, with commercial systems as a supplement and a waiver reported to Congress; Sec. 502 raises the Space Force general officer limit from 21 to 24 (and lowers the Air Force limit from 171 to 168); and Sec. 501 adds Space Force general officer management provisions, including 10 U.S.C. 20110.

uncertainties: The framework document itself and the testimony were not read; DefenseScoop and a secondary summary were used, and the FY2027 total appears as 71.1 billion in the testimony summary and 71.3 billion in CRS. TWZ reports a FY2026 Space Force figure of about 40 billion, which differs from the 31.9 billion CRS gives for FY2026 enacted. Existing offensive systems are classified and not assessed. The general officer increase (21 to 24) and Sec. 1603 were read through the U.S. Code and its amendment notes on law.cornell.edu, because the govinfo.gov text of P.L. 119-60 ends after the table of contents; the notes show no separate effective dates, so the changes are taken as effective on enactment (inference). Whether the Space Force has filled the added general officer positions was not checked. Golden Dome is covered in c04-07 and is not restated.
